CausalChain: Chronic inflammation -> CAF activation -> ECM remodeling and stiffening -> Enhanced mechanotransduction -> YAP/TAZ pathway activation in tumor cells -> Epigenetic reprogramming and promotion of cancer stem cell traits -> Increased chemoresistance
Hypothesis: In cholangiocarcinoma, CAF-induced ECM stiffening activates the YAP/TAZ signaling pathway via mechanotransduction in tumor cells, leading to epigenetic changes that promote cancer stemness and chemoresistance.
Abstract: Recent insights into the tumor microenvironment of cholangiocarcinoma have revealed a complex interplay between chronic inflammation, cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), and tumor cell signaling pathways. We propose that ECM remodeling and stiffening induced by CAF activation create a mechanotransductive niche which activates the YAP/TAZ pathway in cholangiocarcinoma cells. This activation may induce epigenetic modifications that drive cancer stem cell phenotypes and contribute to chemoresistance. Our hypothesis offers a novel perspective on how the physical properties of the tumor microenvironment may reprogram cholangiocarcinoma cells, linking stromal alterations with intracellular epigenetic regulation and suggesting new avenues for therapeutic intervention aimed at disrupting these mechanotransductive circuits.
